books.section: Topic 8.2 The Cold War from 1945 to 1980
Truman and the Beginning of the Cold War (1945-1953)

stimulus.source_note: Aid figures: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian, Marshall Plan figures (approximate). Table compiled for this question from those figures.
stimulus.text:
The table shows the distribution of Marshall Plan aid to Western Europe, 1948-1952, in billions of dollars (approximate).

| Country | Aid received (billions of dollars) |
| United Kingdom | 3.3 |
| France | 2.7 |
| Italy | 1.5 |
| West Germany | 1.4 |
| Netherlands | 1.1 |
| All other recipients | 3.3 |
| Total | about 13 |

source: original; stimulus table compiled from U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian, Marshall Plan figures (approximate)
stem: The Soviet Union's response to the Marshall Plan most directly showed which limit of American policy?

options.text: The plan failed because Congress refused to fund the European rebuilding program.
options.misconception: The table itself proves the funding happened; the money reached Europe.

options.text: Moscow barred Eastern Europe from the aid and built a rival bloc instead.
Western Europeans rejected the Marshall Plan aid as American imperialism.
options.misconception: The aid was taken, not rejected; the table records billions received.

options.text: The plan ended the Cold War between East and West by 1950.
options.misconception: The Cold War continued long past 1950, so the plan did not end it.

rationales.A: Congress funded the plan, and the table shows about $13 billion actually delivered. A refused program could not have paid out those sums.
rationales.B: The Soviet Union forbade Poland and Czechoslovakia to take part and answered with its own aid program for the East. Background from the books: the result was two rival economic blocs, which hardened the division of Europe.
rationales.C: Western Europeans accepted the aid eagerly, and the table shows large sums flowing to Britain, France, and Italy. Rejection would have left the table empty.
rationales.D: The Cold War ran for decades after 1950, through Korea, the missile crisis, and Afghanistan. One aid program did not end it.
rationales.general:
1. The table shows aid flowing only to the West, with no Eastern European country listed among the recipients.
2. Background from the books: That gap is not an accident: Moscow barred its satellites from taking part and built a rival Eastern bloc instead.
3. So the plan's success in the West came with a limit: it deepened the very division of Europe it was meant to heal.
Remember: A policy can succeed on its own side and still fail to cross the line it was drawn against.
